messages.content: The flight schedule is settled enough for this comparison. Change the hotel dates to Saturday through Friday, six nights, and compare the Mission Bay and Coronado properties with real totals. I need to know exactly how the three of us would sleep before we narrow it.
I’ll use Saturday check-in and Friday checkout, with no reservation or hold. Which two properties and room quotes are you looking at?

The Dana on Mission Bay has the Marina View room with two queens. The other is Best Western Plus Suites Hotel Coronado Island, a king suite that says it has a sofa bed and breakfast. Verify that Owen is allowed in the Coronado room and that the sofa bed is actually included, not something we have to request and hope for.

For three guests, including one 12-year-old, both quoted room types allow occupancy without an extra-person charge. At The Dana, the room has two queen beds, so no rollaway is needed. The Coronado king suite is configured with one king bed and one double sofa sleeper; the sofa sleeper is part of the booked room type, though housekeeping should be asked to provide bedding before arrival. Its maximum occupancy is four, and a 12-year-old is included in the three-person quote.
Good. Give me the six-night math line by line. Include every tax, parking charge, resort fee, and anything else mandatory.

The Dana quote is $279 per night for six nights, or $1,674. The resort charge is $42 nightly, totaling $252, and self-parking is $35 nightly, totaling $210. Estimated hotel taxes and assessments are $240.75. The complete six-night cost is $2,376.75. Breakfast is not included. The Coronado suite is $318 per night for six nights, or $1,908. There is no resort fee. Self-parking is $22 nightly, totaling $132. Estimated taxes and assessments are $244.26. The complete cost is $2,284.26, with the hotel’s continental breakfast included for all three guests.
So Coronado is actually $92.49 less after fees, even though the suite quote looked higher than some of the Mission Bay rates.
Correct. Coronado is $92.49 less for the stay, and breakfast is included. The Dana’s two nightly surcharges add $462 before tax, which reverses the apparent base-rate advantage.
Check cancellation deadlines and whether either total is prepaid.

Neither comparison rate is prepaid. The Dana can be canceled without penalty through 4:00 p.m. Pacific time three days before Saturday arrival; after that, the penalty is one night’s room rate plus tax. The Coronado suite can be canceled through 6:00 p.m. Pacific time two days before arrival; after that, the penalty is the first night plus tax. Both require a card guarantee only if reserved, and nothing is being submitted now.
What are the room locations? I care about outdoor access, but I don’t want you throwing out Coronado just because this specific suite lacks a balcony.

The Dana’s Marina View two-queen category can be assigned on an upper floor with a furnished balcony, but the floor and exact view are not guaranteed until assignment. The available Coronado king suite is listed on the first floor and has no private balcony; it opens to the interior corridor rather than directly to a patio. Should I treat that as acceptable for this comparison?

Yes. Going forward on coastal family trips, prioritize a balcony when there is one, but a first-floor room can be perfectly acceptable without it. Don’t eliminate an otherwise good hotel solely over the balcony.
Understood. I’ll keep both here: the balcony strengthens The Dana room, while the first-floor Coronado suite remains viable on its overall merits.
Now compare beach access and the trips we’ll actually make: zoo, airport, Coronado waterfront, and the harbor activities downtown. Use realistic ranges, not one exact number.

From The Dana, the bayfront path and small beach are on the property; reaching an ocean beach around Mission Beach is usually an 8- to 12-minute drive. The San Diego Zoo is roughly 15-25 minutes, the airport 12-20 minutes, Coronado Ferry Landing 20-35 minutes, and the downtown harbor or Embarcadero 15-25 minutes, depending on traffic. From the Coronado hotel, Ferry Landing and the bayfront are about a 7- to 10-minute walk. Coronado Central Beach is approximately 8-12 minutes by car or about 25 minutes on foot. The zoo is generally 15-25 minutes, the airport 15-25 minutes, and the downtown harbor 12-22 minutes by car over the bridge. Ferry service can also reach the Broadway Pier area, but its schedule makes it less useful for a timed airport trip.
Parking ease matters too. Are those both normal in-and-out self-parking rates, and are there destination charges hiding at Coronado?

Yes. The quoted $35 at The Dana and $22 at Coronado are nightly self-parking rates with in-and-out access. Neither quote requires valet parking. The Dana’s $42 resort charge covers items such as property Wi-Fi and selected resort amenities. The Coronado quote has no destination or amenity fee; its mandatory items are the room rate, taxes, and parking already included in the $2,284.26 total.
Breakfast at Coronado: is that actually three people every morning, and what does The Dana cost if we eat there instead of going out?

The Coronado rate includes continental breakfast for all registered occupants, so it covers Marcus, Daniel, and Owen on each of the six mornings. At The Dana, breakfast is à la carte. A practical estimate for three is $55-$75 per morning before tip, or about $330-$450 across six mornings. That would put The Dana at approximately $2,706.75-$2,826.75 before breakfast gratuities, compared with Coronado’s fixed $2,284.26 hotel, parking, and included-breakfast total.
The room layout is the bigger tradeoff. Two real beds is easier than unfolding a sofa every night. How large is the Coronado suite, and can we leave the sofa bed open?

The quoted Coronado suite is approximately 430 square feet, with the king and sitting area in one open room rather than behind a separating door. The sofa sleeper can remain open, but it will narrow the path through the sitting area and reduce daytime seating. The Dana room is approximately 350 square feet; it is smaller overall, but the two queen beds require no nightly conversion and preserve the room’s chair and walking space.

Keep both, but rank Coronado first for now. The lower complete cost, breakfast, and walk to Ferry Landing outweigh the sofa-bed inconvenience. The Dana stays second because of the two queens, balcony possibility, and easier Mission Bay access. Do not reserve either one.

Coronado is now the lead option at $2,284.26 for six nights: king bed, included double sofa sleeper, confirmed occupancy for three including Owen, breakfast for all three, $132 total parking, no resort fee, and free cancellation through 6:00 p.m. Pacific two days before arrival. The Dana remains the alternative at $2,376.75: two queens, possible upper-floor balcony, $210 parking, $252 resort charges, no breakfast, and free cancellation through 4:00 p.m. Pacific three days before arrival. Coronado is $92.49 less before considering its included breakfast. Both travel-time sets and beach-access details remain attached to the comparison. Nothing has been held, reserved, or charged.
